heroHeadline: IDF Strikes Gaza Police Post Killing 5 Officers + Boy; Nuseirat Family Including Infant Killed; France Bans Ben-Gvir; ICC Reportedly Issues 5 New Warrants
heroSubtitle: Israeli forces fired two missiles at a Hamas police post in at-Tawam, northern Gaza on May 23, killing five police officers and a 13-year-old civilian boy, with Hamas accusing Israel of deliberately targeting civil governance to create a security vacuum. On May 24, an Israeli airstrike killed a family of three in Nuseirat refugee camp — Mohammad Abu Mallouh, Alaa Zaqlan, and their 6-month-old infant son Osama. Diplomatically, France imposed a travel ban on National Security Minister Ben-Gvir over his flotilla abuse video, joining Poland and prompting reports that the ICC issued five new sealed warrants targeting Defense Minister Katz, Finance Minister Smotrich (on an apartheid charge), Ben-Gvir, and two IDF commanders. Italy opened a criminal investigation into flotilla detention on allegations of kidnapping and sexual assault. The post-ceasefire Palestinian death toll now exceeds 940+ since the October 2025 ceasefire, with the total since October 7, 2023 surpassing 72,850 documented.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Times of Israel, Haaretz, Bloomberg, Jerusalem Post, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, UNICEF, NPR, Middle East Eye, CNN, The National, Euronews, CBC News, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
